title: refine-gateway-stream-proxy-and-route-payload-policies
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: production customers reported intermittent stream stalls and truncated tool-calling payloads when traffic crosses the OpenAI-compat gateway proxy. This PR tightens routing-based payload limits, adjusts streaming proxy buffer handling, and provides a compatibility shim so function/tool-calling payloads are forwarded reliably between the OpenAI-compat frontend and internal inference routing layers. Scope: 1) Introduce per-route JSON payload size caps and soft-fail semantics for structured-output routes; 2) Replace a fixed-size streaming buffer with an adaptive sliding window that prioritizes flushes for end-of-stream frames and function-calling markers; 3) Add a small compatibility shim that normalizes OpenAI chat/function call envelope differences (content-type variants, chunking boundary markers) without changing backend model contract. Checklist: - [x] add route config schema changes and validation - [x] implement adaptive streaming proxy buffer - [x] compatibility shim for OpenAI envelopes - [x] unit tests for buffer edge cases - [x] integration test across gateway -> router -> runtime - [x] update docs and release notes Notes and constraints: The change intentionally enforces a 1.5MB soft cap on per-request JSON payload for routes labelled openai-compat and structured-output; requests above the soft cap will trigger early advisory errors and suggest chunked uploads or shorter function args. We keep a hard cap at 4MB as a safety net. The adaptive buffer uses measured inter-chunk latency and RSS to decide flush thresholds (configurable via gateway.config.streaming.{min_flush_ms,max_flush_ms,adaptive_threshold}). Backwards compatibility: shim is opt-out via route flag openai_compat_normalize=false for enterprise private deployments that rely on exact byte-forwarding. Related: closes ENG-1845 (stream stall investigation), addresses regression ENG-1910 (function call truncation under load). Rollout plan: staged rollout to canary region for 48 hours with increased sampling on streaming traces; rollback if >0.5% new 5xx or elevated median tail latency on streaming endpoints. Documentation: updated gateway config docs and OpenAI-compat section in the API guide.

review_conversation: Jonah Kim: Can you explain how the soft cap will affect existing users who send large tool args? We should show a clear failure message and a migration path.
Maya Patel: The soft cap emits an advisory 413-with-body that includes recommended chunking pattern and a link to docs. Enterprise private can opt out with openai_compat_normalize=false.
Priya Singh: Tests look good; can the adaptive flush config be tuned at runtime without restart?
Maya Patel: Yes, gateway.config.streaming is hot-reloadable via the config API. Added a note in docs and a unit test for config reload behavior.
Carlos Rivera: Verified in canary: median streaming tail latency down 18% and no function-call truncations during our 30m load test. Approving pending CI finish.
Jonah Kim: Approved after CI green and docs update.
release_notes: Gateway: improved streaming stability and OpenAI-compat function payload handling. Introduced per-route soft payload cap (1.5MB) with 4MB hard cap and an adaptive streaming buffer to reduce stalls and truncations. Default behaviour is conservative and opt-out is available for private installs.
notes_for_release: Backport candidate for release-2026-03 if we see regressions in early canary. Ops: increase streaming trace sampling to 5% during rollout and monitor gateway.streaming.flush_counts metric.
